newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk prosecutor asks for death penalty for 38 Islamists.
newsitem.headline: Turk prosecutor asks for death penalty for 38 Islamists.

text.p: A Turkish prosecutor on Friday demanded the death penalty for 38 Islamists in jail for their involvement in a militant religious riot in which dozens of people died, Anatolian news agency said.
"Prosecutor Hamza Keles asked for the death penalty for 38 suspects in his indictment," the agency said.
The 38 are among around 100 people convicted in 1994 for their part in the riot the previous year in the central town of Sivas. They had been jailed for up to 15 years in an earlier court rule.

But the appeals court overruled the original decision last year and demanded that many of the accused be retried on the more serious charge of trying to change the state's constitutional order by using arms.
Anatolian said the prosecutor asked for sentences of up to 15 years for 40 of the other convicts and the acquittal of a further 14.
Rioters set fire to a hotel in Sivas, killing 37 people. Most victims were writers and singers attending a cultural festival organised by the Alevi sect, a liberal branch of Islam.
Death penalties are still given by Turkish courts but no execution has been carried out for more than 10 years.
Turkey's judiciary has been cracking down on Islamists in a campaign against religious activism that helped topple the government of former prime minister Necmettin Erbakan last month.
Three Islamist journalists face more than a year in jail after they were alleged to have insulted a prosecutor for his attempts to ban the pro-Islamist Welfare Party.

"A case was opened against me and two of our reporters on Thursday because we criticised the Appeal Court's chief prosecutor in a news story," Ali Ihsan Karahasanoglu, editor of the Akit newspaper, told Reuters.
The prosecutor, Vural Savas, asked the Constitutional Court in May to close Welfare after the party was alleged to have tried to change Turkey's secular system.
Welfare is led by Erbakan, who became Turkey's first Islamist prime minister last year.
Karahasanoglu denied insulting the prosecutor. He said the paper had criticised Savas for holding a news conference about the Welfare case.
